chunks: Abu Basir asked him about a woman who dies: who has the greatest right to perform the funeral prayer over her? He said:
"Her husband." He said to him: Does the husband have more right than the father, the child, and the brother? He said: "Yes, and he washes her."

And my father, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his letter to me: Know, my son, that the person most entitled to the prayer over the deceased is the one whom the guardian of the deceased puts forward. If there is a man from Banu Hashim among the people, then he has the greater right to pray over him if the guardian of the deceased puts him forward. If someone steps forward without being put forward by the guardian of the deceased, then he is usurping.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ: more entitled or having stronger legal priority
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the funeral prayer performed over the deceased
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا: her husband, identified here as having primary entitlement
key_terms.غَاصِبٌ: one who wrongfully takes a right that belongs to another
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْمَيِّتِ: the guardian of the deceased who appoints the prayer leader
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُهَا: he washes her body for burial

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to lead the funeral prayer for a deceased woman in Shi'a fiqh?
ai.summary: This text states that the husband has the strongest claim to perform the funeral prayer over his deceased wife and may also wash her body. It also establishes that leadership of the funeral prayer belongs to the one appointed by the deceased's guardian, and that precedence without such appointment is considered an unlawful usurpation of that right.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.474 - Abu Basir asked Imam (as) about who has the most right to perform the funeral prayer for a woman who has passed away.
Imam (as) replied: "Her husband."

Abu Basir then asked: "Does the husband have more right than her father, son, or brother?"
The Imam said: "Yes, and he may also wash her."

[AL SADUQ]
My father wrote in his message to me:
"Know, my son, that the person with the most right to lead the funeral prayer for the deceased is whoever is designated by the deceased's guardian (Wali). If there is a man from the Banu Hashim among the people, he has priority for leading the prayer if designated by the guardian of the deceased. If someone leads without being appointed by the deceased’s guardian, then they are usurping that right."
